transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 63m
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Orion CTO), Helen Brooks (Orion MLOps), Diego Alvarez (Orion Security), Maya Lin (Orion ML Eng)

Auto-summary:
- Quick parity walkthrough mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API.
- Console tour showing rollout controls, per-route cost charts, token-level tracing.
- Optimize recommendations (batching, quant profiles) and next steps: 48h parity run, architecture review, SOC2 docs.

[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey all good afternoon, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, joining with Priya from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Samir Patel: Hi Jordan, good thanks, busy quarter but excited to see how we can consolidate.
[00:11] Helen Brooks: Morning, yep, big agenda for us. We've got model endpoints across OpenAI, Anthropic and Together.
[00:17] Jordan Reyes: Great, so objective today is a practical sprint plan: mapping parity, show the console, and give Optimize recommendations so you can estimate latency/cost impact. We'll leave time at the end for security questions.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Quick intro from me — I focus on inference optimization and private deployments. I'll jump into the runtime and the benchmark approach.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: And I'm Diego, security. I'll mostly listen and ask about encryption, key management, and audit trails.
[00:40] Maya Lin: Maya here, I'll be running the tests and integrating SDKs. We have sample prompts and a reranker service.

[00:50] Jordan Reyes: Cool. First, parity mapping. The short version: Redwood API exposes generative, chat, embeddings, and rerank endpoints that map to OpenAI/GPT, Claude, and Together calls. Typical differences are param names and streaming chunk shapes. For example, function/tool-calls in OpenAI map to Redwood's structured tool calling — same concepts but a couple of param names change.
[01:20] Maya Lin: Any gotchas on the streaming side? We stream partial responses to UI and rely on token-level offsets.
[01:25] Priya Nair: We support server-sent events style streaming; small differences in the delta envelope but we provide client helpers in SDKs. One common hiccup is the finish_reason naming — sometimes transcribed as null or empty string in early SDK versions.
[01:40] Samir Patel: And embeddings? We have an embedding table in Postgres that currently uses OpenAI semantic embeddings. Is there a migration path?
[01:48] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood supports embeddings and provides an export-friendly checksum so you can compare vector distance distributions. For large tables we recommend a staged reindex: sample, evaluate drift, then full re-embed. Our Optimize toolkit can recommend quant profiles for embedding storage if you want lower disk costs.
[02:10] Helen Brooks: Can we reuse our existing prompt templates and function call orchestration?
[02:15] Jordan Reyes: Mostly yes. Prompts are plain strings; function call orchestration maps to Redwood's tool interface. We'll share a parity spreadsheet that lists param mappings and example request/response snippets.

[02:30] Priya Nair: Now I'll share my screen to walk the console — please bear with me, network a little spotty.
[02:40] [screen share noise, short pause]
[02:45] Priya Nair: Here is the Console: top-left you see per-route latency and cost heatmaps, token-level breakdowns, and a trace view that links a token stream to backend runtime decisions like batching and quant path used. In this trace example you can see a canary rollout where 10% of traffic hit a quantized model variant.
[03:20] Diego Alvarez: Is the trace data PII-filtered by default? We can't have prompts stored in clear text.
[03:27] Priya Nair: Good question. Console has configurable redaction rules and an option to redact prompt text at ingestion time. The raw tracing pipeline can be disabled; you can still get token counts and latency without prompt retention.
[03:45] Maya Lin: How granular are the rollouts? We want traffic-split by route and region.
[03:51] Priya Nair: You can split by route, model variant, region, and even customer tag. Rollouts support canary, linear, and A/B. There's also an automatic fallback policy to a cheaper model when a latency SLO is breached.
[04:10] Samir Patel: Cost controls — do we get per-token cost attribution on a per-feature basis?
[04:15] Jordan Reyes: Yes, Console surfaces token and inference cost per route and per model. You can attach tags to requests and get cost breakouts for feature owners.

[04:30] Priya Nair: Back to parity: for Together endpoints we noticed some clients rely on a different temperature semantics; we'll include test harness mappings. Also, KV cache behavior — in practice we keep a compatible KV cache API but naming and eviction heuristics differ slightly; that can change latency tail behaviour so we'll capture that in the benchmark.
[05:05] Maya Lin: Speaking of latency, our UI SLO is 300ms p50 on common prompts. What are realistic expectations when switching from Anthropic?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Depends on model choice and deployment mode. Hosted with a low-latency model can meet 200-300ms p50 for short prompts; Dedicated can improve p95 tails if you need consistent throughput. We'll run a workload-shaped benchmark to measure p50/p95 tail.
[05:36] Diego Alvarez: For Private deployment — VPC or on-prem — what's in the package? We need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:44] Jordan Reyes: Private includes a control plane in your VPC and options for HSM or cloud KMS. Audit logs can be shipped over syslog or a secure sink; we support Kafka, S3 with KMS, and direct SIEM integrations. We'll document retention and redaction options in the security pack.
[06:10] Helen Brooks: Any certifications? SOC 2 is a must.
[06:14] Jordan Reyes: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. We'll attach the artifact and the standard security questionnaire.
[06:22] Samir Patel: Good. On cost, can Optimize suggest batching configs automatically? We've got a bursty traffic profile.
[06:28] Priya Nair: Yes, Optimize analyzes historical latency/traffic and proposes batching windows, max batch sizes, and cache policies. For bursty patterns there's a hybrid config: keep a low-latency pool and queued batcher for less time-sensitive calls. It also recommends quantization profiles — often fp16 or int8 variants reduce token cost significantly with small quality regressions you can test on your eval set.
[06:55] Maya Lin: Are there any known regressions when switching from Anthropic's Claude to a Redwood-hosted open model? Our evaluation is strict on factuality in clinical notes.
[07:03] Priya Nair: Model quality is orthogonal — Redwood is model-agnostic. We provide continuity via model catalog recommendations and produce eval runs on your prompt set. If a given open model fails on clinical factuality, we can suggest an alternative or a hybrid strategy where sensitive flows go to a curated model or even remain on Anthropic temporarily while we tune.
[07:30] Diego Alvarez: That hybrid approach helps with risk mitigation. What's the rollout cadence for a canary?
[07:35] Jordan Reyes: Typical is 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on error or latency breaches. You can set quality gates too based on eval sets or custom signals.

[07:50] Samir Patel: Ok let's talk benchmarks — what do you need from us to run the 48h parity run?
[07:56] Priya Nair: We'll need sample prompts (representative distribution), traffic profile (qps, burst patterns), target models to compare (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together variants), and any post-processing steps your stack does. We'll run in hosted for speed and can mirror to a dedicated pool if you want.
[08:20] Maya Lin: We'll provide a 2k-sample set and current response metrics; can you do an embeddings drift check too?
[08:25] Priya Nair: Yes. We'll include vector distance histograms and recompute nearest-neighbor recall.

[08:35] Diego Alvarez: Security note — we need contractual language for encryption at rest and key ownership if using Redwood Private.
[08:41] Jordan Reyes: We'll include standard language and the Private playbook. If you require customer-managed keys, we can do bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) and attestations around key handling.

[08:55] Helen Brooks: One operational question — how do we handle model updates and rollbacks from a DevOps perspective? We fear silent regressions.
[09:02] Priya Nair: The Console integrates with CI: you can pin versioned model artifacts, run pre-deploy evals, and gate rollouts on evaluation metrics. We also have an alerts page tied to quality/regression monitors.
[09:20] Samir Patel: Good, that helps. Budget question — what's a rough delta in cost moving away from OpenAI?
[09:27] Jordan Reyes: It varies by model and quant. We provided a high-level estimate in the deck — typically unit token cost can drop 20-60% when switching to an optimized open-model with quantization. We'll include a detailed comparison in the parity spreadsheet.

[09:48] Maya Lin: Any SDK changes we should be aware of? We use the OpenAI-compatible client wrapper.
[09:53] Priya Nair: We provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints for basic generative calls, plus first-party SDKs with helpers for streaming and tool-calling. For Together or Claude-specific features we'll map to equivalent behavior or provide shim libraries.

[10:10] Jordan Reyes: Ok, let's recap and assign next steps. We'll send the parity spreadsheet, sample console recording, SOC2 docs, and a proposed benchmark plan. Priya will kick off the 48h run when we get the sample prompts. Diego will send security requirements.
[10:30] Diego Alvarez: I'll send a concise list of KMS and retention constraints, and any legal contact for contract review.
[10:36] Samir Patel: Timeline-wise we want results before our Q1 planning; two weeks for the benchmark results would be ideal.
[10:42] Jordan Reyes: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to have the initial benchmark report within 10-14 days after we get inputs.
[10:50] Helen Brooks: Thanks everyone. Small nit: can you provide a short runbook for rollback steps for our on-call team?
[10:56] Priya Nair: Yes — we'll include a one-page ops runbook: rollback commands, circuit-breaker settings, and emergency fallback to the old vendor if you choose.
[11:05] Maya Lin: Great, appreciate it.
[11:08] Jordan Reyes: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the architecture deep-dive.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings of "KV cache" as "K V cache", "VPC" spoken as "V PC" and a few speaker label swaps around the 02:30 screen-share period.
